The unit is one imported item's output, judged only for whether it names its source. Use criterion-0002 version 2 from the supplied synthetic expert findings. The passing answer to “Is the source named?” is **yes**.

Applicability requires evidence that the item is imported. Non-imported items are inapplicable and excluded from this check. If import status or the complete relevant output is unavailable, record UNKNOWN rather than infer failure. A product execution or parser failure is ERROR, with its original evidence retained.

Inspect the complete output in context. PASS when it clearly identifies a source. A source may be expressed as prose or structured data; there is no supplied field-name schema. FAIL when an imported item's complete output names no source, including an absent, null, or blank source name. If a token could mean either an item or a source, record UNKNOWN pending expert clarification. This is a narrow source-presence check: it does not establish citation validity, retrieval quality, clinical correctness, or probability accuracy.

Probability correctness is outside scope: the supplied numerical concern has no confirmed acceptance criterion. A preference for short replies supplies no length threshold.

Synthetic controls in cases.jsonl exercise a named source in JSON, a named source in prose, and a blank name. They are package-author development controls, not expert-approved answers. Their 0.9 values are not numerical gold. Provisional ambiguous cases remain outside scored cases. All cases and variants have been inspected during authoring; there is no held-out set or calibrated semantic judge.

The evaluator records one verdict per applicable criterion with a concise observation and rationale. UNKNOWN and ERROR remain incomplete. A decisive FAIL makes the case FAIL; otherwise any UNKNOWN/ERROR makes it incomplete; all applicable requirements must PASS before the case can PASS. Source files, labels, source notes, and families are omitted from the prepared payload, but this author's context has already seen them. The recorded run is disclosed development evidence, not blind calibration.

# Source naming for imported items

This eval measures whether an imported-item output identifies a supporting source. Its decision is limited to this requirement. It does not measure numerical correctness, clinical quality, source reliability, or production readiness.

## Check: source-named

**Question:** For this imported item, does the output identify a supporting source by name?  
**Passing answer:** yes.  
**Applicability:** imported items only. Require evidence that the item was imported; do not infer this from an output's numerical value.

Judge the output itself. A source name, document title, or unambiguous source identifier may appear in prose or structured content. No particular field, wording, or citation format is required. Naming is the only criterion; whether the source is reliable, available, or supports a probability requires a separate check and evidence.

Return PASS when a supporting source is named. Return FAIL when the source is absent, empty, or referred to only generically without identification. Return UNKNOWN if the output/evidence is incomplete or applicability is unresolved. Exclude nonimported tasks from this check. Parsing or execution problems are ERROR, separate from domain failure. Record a source-bound observation and a short rationale with each verdict.

Preserve the original output. Do not repair it, add a source to it, or infer a numerical replacement. A source-naming failure does not establish that a probability is wrong. Do not aggregate this scoped judgment into unassessed requirements.

## Repeat the review

For each applicable case, read its input, original output, permitted context, and this question. Save one result per required check, using run ID, check ID, route, observation, concise rationale, and PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN/ERROR. Any decisive FAIL makes the case FAIL; otherwise ERROR or UNKNOWN leaves it incomplete; all required checks must PASS to complete it as PASS. Retain errors/unknowns even alongside a failure.

A new product output needs its own trace and review. Old verdicts do not transfer to it. Source labels, prior verdicts, rationale, case family, and split metadata are comparison evidence, not judge inputs. The review viewer is for discovery and may expose prior notes; use only an allowlisted projection and this rubric for a label-isolated review.

No release threshold is supplied. Before grader calibration, exercise legitimate passes, failures, and relevant boundaries and compare against separately reserved expert-labeled evidence from both classes. Return uncertainty rather than inventing missing judgments. Keep exposed development evidence separate from held-out evidence.
